active_release_candidate.purpose: reconcile runtime-only 0.1.28-0.1.30 work into main, repair confirmed regressions, and prove critical invariants again after each lifecycle transition

current_goal.goal: Restore main as the only development truth and make every critical invariant re-confirm itself after the lifecycle transitions that can invalidate its previous evidence.
non_goals: Do not change the model-card Video ownership contract.
Do not introduce cross-channel fallback between Ark and Agent Plan.
Do not build a second static global model-capability/context database inside the plugin.
Do not claim marketplace or Windows verification from repository CI.

active_validation_frontier.name: negative_lifecycle_counterexample_closure
next_actions: Re-run Runtime Distribution Gate with both preserved 0.1.25 negative transport contracts and new 0.1.31 lifecycle-policy contracts.
Run the real AstrBot 4.27.3 lifecycle matrix through plugin-config hot reload, provider rebind, process restart, same-version replacement and uninstall.
Re-run model-card Video, lifecycle and 0.1.19 compatibility workflows after the negative-case fixes.
Only after every current-head blocking workflow is green may the candidate move to ready/releaseable.
observed: The first 0.1.31 candidate reached all-green Runtime Distribution, Video, Lifecycle and 0.1.19 compatibility workflows.
That all-green state did not prove every later lifecycle transition because confirmations have scope and lifetime.
Agent Plan ark-code-latest is a dynamic routing alias, so its visible model name cannot safely identify one fixed context window.
Writing plugin-family context values before AstrBot resolution can suppress more accurate host LLM metadata and can also confuse total model window with the input-history compression guard.
The first 0.1.31 image guard ran after AstrBot native image Base64 materialization, so it protected the upstream byte ceiling but not pre-Base64 memory expansion.
The first 0.1.31 test rewrite replaced several 0.1.25 video negative-path assertions instead of retaining them as an independent evidence layer.
AstrBot plugin-config save performs an in-process plugin reload; existing Provider instances have a separate lifecycle and must be explicitly rebound to new media/cache policy.
Audio transcoding previously read the entire output file before enforcing the configured byte ceiling.

stable_boundaries: AstrBot owns provider lifecycle, fallback, retry, model-card management, shared Dashboard schema and host model metadata.
The plugin owns Volcengine protocol adaptation and must not maintain a second global capability/context database.
Video remains a native per-model-card modalities choice scoped only to Ark and Agent Plan Source types.
Ordinary Ark and Agent Plan keep separate fixed endpoints and credentials; the plugin never silently crosses channels.
Explicit positive max_context_tokens values are host/model-card input-guard configuration; the plugin does not infer them from broad model-name families.
Dynamic aliases, endpoint IDs and unknown models do not receive plugin-guessed context windows.
A confirmation is valid only for its object/state/lifecycle node; transitions that can invalidate it require a new confirmation.
Older negative-path contracts remain independently executable when later releases add new tests.
Runtime is generated from main; direct runtime development is not an accepted steady state.
warning: 0.1.31 remains validating and is not installable. Stable user installations remain on runtime 0.1.30 until the negative lifecycle counterexample matrix is green on the current head and the guarded publisher promotes a ready candidate.
